subject.title: Cron: agent runs that self-report ===DONE_ERR=== are recorded as ok — failureAlert never fires

question: Should OpenClaw make `===DONE_ERR===` a supported core terminal failure sentinel for isolated cron agent output, or keep cron failures limited to structured and known runtime-denial signals?
rationale: The present classifier intentionally accepts a bounded marker set; adding this application-level convention changes the public meaning of assistant text and may affect existing jobs.

options.title: Adopt a narrow terminal sentinel
options.body: Recognize only an exact final non-empty `===DONE_ERR===` line, document it as a cron contract, and add status plus failure-alert regression coverage.

options.title: Keep structured outcomes only
options.body: Leave core classification unchanged and advise job owners to emit runtime-structured errors or use external monitoring for application-level completion signals.

options.title: Track it with final-outcome work
options.body: Fold the decision into the canonical final-assistant outcome discussion if its linked implementation is expanded to define the same contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt a narrow terminal sentinel
recommendation.body: Recognize only an exact final non-empty `===DONE_ERR===` line, document it as a cron contract, and add status plus failure-alert regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the existing bounded cron-denial classification and its documented semantics.
